title: A faster clock accumulates a gap
hook: Start two toy clocks together and prescribe different reading rates.

doesNotKnow: Distinguish an initial offset from a gap accumulated by different rates.

misconception: Starting together forces clocks to continue agreeing regardless of rates.
objective: Distinguish an initial offset from a gap accumulated by different rates.

claims.text: Elapsed time can differ between clocks in different physical conditions.
Carlo Rovelli, The Order of Time (2018)
The prescribed rates give {A} and {B}. Matching initial readings do not prevent an accumulating gap when rates differ.
Does it hold up? This integrates prescribed readings only. No relativity equation, gravitational effect or clock measurement is supplied.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: Clocks start at zero and advance 2 and 3 ticks per reference step. After four steps, what is their gap?
recall.why: Readings are 8 and 12; their gap is 4.
